name: Red Hat Ecosystem
description:
A Unified Methodology for Red Hat Partner Success
A unified strategic framework detailing how Red Hat aligns, enables, and scales ecosystem partners through structured planning, verified technical capability, and iterative market execution.

narratives.name: Red Hat Ecosystem Partner Unified Methodology
narratives.description:
Red Hat cannot scale business growth by relying only on our internal delivery teams and direct sales. To expand our market reach without proportionally raising our support costs, we must build a robust partner ecosystem that acts as a scalable revenue channel.

To achieve this, we use a single, unified methodology that transforms partners from delivery-dependent relationships into self-sufficient growth channels. This methodology connects business planning, technical enablement, and market execution into a continuous operational lifecycle.

narrativeContexts.context:
Partner Account Managers (PAMs) often face immense complexity when managing strategic relationships across our ecosystem. Without a standardized planning framework, joint activities can become reactive, leading to missed revenue targets and inconsistent relationship quality.

To bring order to this complexity, PAMs collaborate with partners to build comprehensive Partner Success Plans (PSPs). These plans align growth expectations between Red Hat and our partners, define joint business initiatives, secure executive sponsorship, and establish data-driven milestones to track progress.

PAMs execute this strategy using a structured nine-step methodology managed directly within Red Hat Sales Cloud (RHSC). This workflow guides PAMs and partners to:
* Conduct a thorough partner business analysis.
* Brainstorm collaborative growth initiatives.
* Establish clear, measurable objectives.
* Map executive sponsorship across both organizations to ensure long-term commitment.
* Host regular quarterly business reviews (QBRs) to maintain alignment and address challenges early.

Transitioning from ad-hoc communication to structured success planning helps turn complex partnerships into predictable business relationships, laying the foundation for deep technical engagement.

Once strategic alignment is established, we focus on technical execution. Many partners remain in delivery-dependent relationships, requiring hands-on support from Red Hat teams to complete customer projects. Our goal is to shift these partners toward self-sufficiency. When partners can deliver solutions independently, they generate sustained, predictable revenue for both their business and ours.

To guide partners through this operational shift, we use a structured capability validation model called Technical Engagement Planning (TEP). This model follows a practical "Crawl-Walk-Run" maturity framework to build partner confidence:
* Crawl (The Technical Win): We establish partner commitment and validate their foundational alignment with Red Hat technologies.
* Walk (Initial Delivery): We support the partner through their first real-world deployments, building practical capability while gradually reducing their reliance on Red Hat support.
* Run (TDP Achievement): The partner achieves a validated Technical Decision Point (TDP). At this stage, they can design, deploy, and support Red Hat solutions autonomously.

By maturing our partner channels through this systematic validation, we lower our overall cost to serve (CSERV). TDP-validated partners are fully equipped to expand our geographic and market presence without requiring ongoing, hands-on engineering support from Red Hat.

A technically validated partner is ready to go to market. Ecosystem marketing teams identify new business opportunities that align with Red Hat technical decision points, assess partner marketing capabilities, and design targeted campaigns.

Successful demand generation requires close, cross-functional collaboration. Red Hat and partner teams work together to build relevant campaign content and enable partner sales representatives. By establishing clear roles and responsibilities using a Responsibility Assignment Matrix (RACI), we ensure everyone knows who is responsible and accountable before any campaign goes live.

Once prepared, partners execute multi-channel campaigns using digital marketing, educational events, and direct outreach to identify qualified opportunities. Throughout the execution phase, Red Hat teams provide co-selling support and conduct weekly check-ins to monitor campaign health.

After the campaign finishes, we measure overall performance and analyze our joint Return on Investment (ROI). The cross-functional teams host a retrospective meeting to document lessons learned. These insights flow directly back into the Phase 1 planning cycle, creating a continuous improvement loop that makes our shared marketing efforts increasingly effective over time.
